alias: Cameras - a monitor has stopped updating
description: Freshness dead-man for the four camera monitors. Every other dead-man here triggers only on unavailable/unknown/-1, and NONE of them looks at age - which left a whole failure class invisible. Home Assistant rewrites last_updated only when the state or an attribute CHANGES, and a healthy fleet emits a byte-identical payload for hours, so a monitor whose update loop has STOPPED sits pinned at "9 / 0.0 / 9/9 OK" indefinitely: no bad state, no recorder row, no page. Measured before the fix, sensor.camera_health had already gone 37 minutes without a row while perfectly healthy, and legitimate steady periods reach 1h56m (health) and 2h20m (flap) - which is why a naive age bar would false-fire, and why each script now publishes a bucketed `updated_at` so last_updated advances at least once per 600s bucket whenever the loop actually runs. Bars are per sensor because poll intervals differ 15x: 45 min for the three fast monitors, 90 min for the 30-minute motion monitor. Re-asserts hourly at :17 as a restart-wipe guard, and pushes on anything except that re-assert.

data.title: 📷 Camera monitor stopped updating
